articleTitle: Harmonics in power systems
abstract: Thyristor-produced harmonics in power systems are gaining increased importance because of the interference and disturbance they cause. Particularly vulnerable are weak power systems and communication systems in close proximity to such power systems. This author presents some actual situations that have been encountered and the remedial measures employed to overcome these harmonic disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric melting of crystal glass
abstract: The cost of electricity with respect to gas or oil is high over most of the industrial world, and according to present forecasts, will remain so for at least the next decade. Despite this fact many sectors of the glass producers have turned away from traditional melting methods (utilising gas or oil) and have focused their attention on the use of electricity. The use of electric melting processes has had a particular impact in the field of lead-crystal production. Dramatic changes have occurred as old equipment and even older working practices have had to be abandoned. This revolution, that started in Europe, has now come to the United Kingdom.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving generator availability by use of strategic spares
abstract: In order to improve the availability of its large high-merit generating units, the UK electricity-supply industry has developed a strategy of holding major strategic spare components. These are deployed in the event of failures or when required to expedite overhauls or modifications. Displaced major components are then repaired, refurbished or modified while the unit remains in service. Analysis techniques which can be used to evaluate the likely capabilities of one, two or more spare components for a particular plant family were also developed and the basis of these is described. the author describes the application of the strategies to generator components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress in tidal power
abstract: There has been much activity in tidal power in the UK over the last two years, with a range of site-specific studies and generic studies completed or in progress, several being part funded by industry. A major conference is to be held in November 1989 to present the results. The author looks at the background to the work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flue-gas desulphurisation-Drax: the first UK retrofit
abstract: In 1987 it was decided that Drax would be the first UK power station to be fitted with flue-gas desulphurisation equipment. Drax is the largest UK power station (4000 MW) and the largest coal-fired station in Western Europe. Work has now started on the FGD installation which, when completed in 1996, will be the largest in the world. The author discusses the reasons for choosing Drax and the limestone/gypsum FGD process. The installation of the system, the changes in the electrical system and the control and instrumentation are discussed. The civil work and project information are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power-station refurbishment within the CEGB
abstract: Studies to investigate the technical and economic feasibility of running the CEGB coal-fired plant in excess of their original design lives (100/150000 operating hours) have shown substantial cost advantages compared to building new plant. An in-depth life assessment has been carried out for all major power-plant components at each coal-fired power station. This has highlighted the investment profile required to achieve lives of up to 45 years which for some 500 MW generating units corresponds to in excess of 300000 operating hours. The studies have led the CEGB to implement a programme of progressive refurbishment which maximises the commercial value of existing plant. It is based on component replacement within the statutory and planned overhaul periods of generating plant. The authors describe the CEGB management and technical approach to power-station refurbishment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Steel-tube reheating
abstract: In integrated iron and steel works, fuel gases are produced as byproducts of the coke, iron and steelmaking processes, and can be utilised to fuel reheat furnaces and to generate steam and thus power. British Steel Tubes, while producing some steel in electric arc furnaces, is, in the main, supplied with the raw materials for tubemaking by other steel works. All energy is therefore purchased as fuel oil, natural gas and electrical power. Efficient energy usage is thus essential to the cost effectiveness of the value-adding process of tubemaking. The authors discuss the efficient use of energy for steel-tube reheating at the electric weld stretch reducing plant in the British Steel Tube Works at Corby.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The great dielectric phenomenon
abstract: With the expansion of demand immediately after the First World War, serious problems arose in the design of dielectric insulation for high-voltage cables. The author describes these problems and highlights many of the efforts made to overcome them. He describes the failure mechanisms of such dielectrics and examines the research which was carried out to determine failure causes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Energy conservation in Pakistan: a unified approach
abstract: With high population growth and rapidly growing economies, many developing countries are not able to meet the rapidly rising demand for electricity, leading to power shortages and restraints on future growth. The authors show that one way of closing the 'energy gap' is a nationally planned programme of energy conservation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prospects for alternative-energy sources in electricity generation
abstract: After the first oil-price shock in the early 1970s, the CEGB initiated a programme to establish the prospects for electricity production from alternative-energy sources. The sharpening of interest in the environmental benefits of alternative-energy sources has added impetus to the work. The CEGB programme includes research and engineering studies on tidal, wave, geothermal, hydro, biomass and wind. The author discusses the prospects for each of these energy sources. One of the most promising resources is wind power. The author discusses this option in more detail including the prospects for offshore wind turbines. Environmental concerns are also mentioned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The nuclear programme
abstract: Sizewell B, the first of a proposed small series of PWR power stations, is now under construction. A project organisation has been established to undertake the proposed programme, and planning applications are at various stages for the other three PWRs. The follow-on PWRs will replicate the Sizewell B design. The author discusses the nuclear programme adopted by the CEGB and describes the work on Sizewell B. The follow on PWRs are planned for Hinckley Point C, Wylfa B, and Sizewell C. The benefits of replicating the Sizewell B design are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control and automation of the Manchester to Liverpool sludge pipeline of the North West Water Authority. I
abstract: The sludge pipeline scheme, enabling the transfer of the Authority's sludge shipping operation to the new Liverpool Sewage Treatment Works, consists of five pumping stations operating in series, with variable speed control to suit the varying hydraulic requirements. It is an example of a fully integrated automation system in the water industry, using communicating PLCs. The author discusses the design of the pipeline and then goes on to describe the power systems for each of the fine pumping stations and the variable speed drives using synchronous motors and static thyristor convertors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-head hydroelectric power using pneumatic conversion
abstract: New hydroelectric power installations at low-head river sites are often an uneconomic proposition using conventional water turbines. The author deals with alternative power-conversion systems based on air as an intermediate fluid which are aimed at achieving a more economic solution to the problem. A novel water-to-air power-conversion system has been built at Borrowash on the River Derwent which utilises a flexible membrane as a self-oscillating interface between water and air to drive an air turbine and generator. Problems of this new technology are discussed and a number of improvements are proposed which should lead to a viable and economic alternative to conventional low-head hydro stations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote techniques for inspection and refurbishment of nuclear plant
abstract: The author reviews remote and inspection techniques, for nuclear power plant maintenance and repair, discussed at a conference. The remote techniques include the use of robots and manipulators, the inspection techniques include both visual and nondestructive tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in electric traction
abstract: Railways are in a competitive business sector and need to keep up with the latest developments in technology. The author reviews recent developments of traction equipment for HV AC supply systems and DC supplied railways, and finally looks at inverter-fed induction motor drives which are increasingly being used on both AC and DC supplies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments on British Railways traction and rolling stock
abstract: The success of any railway operation depends on efficient and reliable trains. British Rail operates 10335 route miles of which 3681 miles are electrified at 25 kV AC and 2715 at 750 V DC third rail. The author looks at the developments in power and control electronics which have ensured that trains function reliably and successfully.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Static VAR compensators and their applications in Australia
abstract: Static VAr compensators (SVCs) do not have inertia or any major moving or rotating components so they are very fast at responding to changing network conditions. SVCs have been used to solve a variety of problems on the Australian HV/power systems because of their fast response and versatility. The author discusses some of these applications to large transmission and distribution systems in Australia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Induction heating with transverse flux in strip-metal process lines
abstract: The processing of metal strip is a vast industry, providing material for such diverse fields of application as steel automobile panels and aluminium cans. At some time in its production history the strip is usually heated. Induction heating, with its excellent controllability and response, is unequalled for the heating of metal at very high power density. Its application in transverse flux mode utilising electricity efficiently at megawatt power levels is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electricity supplies for Addu Atoll
abstract: The authors assess the rehabilitation requirements of power plant and power supplies for the public electricity undertakings of the Maldives Electricity Board in Male, the capital of the Republic of Maldives, and in particular Addu Atoll. The Maldives Electricity Board (MEB) is a Government owned organisation established in 1982. It is the statutory body responsible for public electricity supplies throughout the Republic of Maldives and responsible to the office of the President. The MEB systems operate at a frequency of 50 Hz and the voltages in use are 11 kV, 3.3 kV and 0.4 kV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric-assisted drying and processing
abstract: In dielectric heating, water is selectively heated whenever it is dispersed within a body. As this form of heating does not depend on transfer through a surface, significant improvements in heating and drying rates can improve product quality. The author looks at microwave and radio frequency heating and their applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control and automation of the Manchester to Liverpool sludge pipeline of the North West Water Authority. II
abstract: For pt.I see ibid., vol.3, no.4, p.225 (1989). The author looks at the scheme for the construction of a 58 km pipeline to pump sewage sludge from Manchester to Liverpool via a total of five pumping stations with an additional input of sludge at Warrington Sewage Works. Each pumping station has its own dedicated processor in the form of a programmable logic controller (PLC) to start, stop and control the complete pumping station operation. The whole pipeline performs as a fully integrated system on automatic control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some aspects of bidding for major electrical substation plant
abstract: Major electrical substation plants can be worth a great deal of money to a company, so when one is required by the electricity supply authority a number of companies will bid to construct it. The author looks at the bid documents, inspection to ensure standards, maintenance and financial aspects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Service experience of large substation transformers in Australia
abstract: Substation transformers constitute a significant portion of the overall capital investment in a large transmission system. Stringent but realistic requirements on performance and testing need to be clearly understood and specified. To ensure reliable in-service performance, the technical requirements must be supplemented by adequate quality-assurance systems during design and manufacture, and an effective maintenance system during service. The author gives a broad overview of more than three decades of in-service experience with various types of substation transformers by the Electricity Commission of New South Wales, Australia. The author describes technical, testing and quality requirements and discusses aspects of transformer operation, in-service performance and failures. The author also examines some aspects of transformer maintenance, particularly diagnostic techniques for early fault detection in ageing transformers, and the impact of some technological developments on design and performance of HV and EHV power transformers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-voltage auxiliary switchgear for power stations
abstract: Air-break switchgear has been used extensively for many years to control station auxiliaries. Vacuum and SF/sub 6/ techniques, already well established in the distribution field, are now being applied for the higher ratings and more onerous duties of switchgear in large fossil-fired and nuclear power stations. The author discusses power plant auxiliary systems and the environmental, mechanical and electrical operating conditions of the switchgear. The author then describes in detail the criteria affecting the choice of appropriate switchgear for auxiliaries. The choice of operating mechanisms and special requirements for nuclear power stations are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transmission operations and maintenance experience of China Light & Power Co
abstract: Transmission-equipment performance and operational difficulties associated with the supply of electricity to the densely populated areas of Kowloon is reviewed. The performance of gas-insulated switchgear is considered from its initial introduction in 1974 and is compared to internationally recognised statistics from which service experience and future developments are summarised. Information relating to power cable developments, fault statistic analysis and how these are influenced by the Hong Kong environment are discussed. The author attempts to embrace all these areas and give the reader an insight into the methods employed, and difficulties encountered, in retaining transmission availability in Hong Kong.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pros and cons of paper and polymeric insulated cables
abstract: With the availability of both paper and polymeric insulated cables many engineers still find themselves uncertain as to the correct choice to make when deciding which cable to install on their system, be it low or high voltage. The reason for this probably lies in the welter of information that has been produced. This information, which covers international test data and operational experience, present and future availability of materials, production and to some extent trade skills, sometimes appears to be contradictory and biased. It originates from a wide variety of sources. The authors list the advantages and disadvantages of paper-insulated cables so that they can be referred to judiciously when detailed consideration of polymeric cables is being carried out. This will reduce the possibility of engineers overlooking what they already have and changing for the sake of change to a 'modern' cable without giving the issue the objective judgment that engineers are expected to (and indeed usually) provide. They summarise the position of polymeric cable and compare it with traditional paper-insulated cable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power generation by geothermal energy and its possible application in the UK
abstract: Power generation from diverse renewable energy sources has been a major objective of government supported energy research programmes around the world for more than a decade. However, despite the attention to a wide range of technologies, only geothermal energy and some forms of hydro power have now reached the maturity needed to compete commercially with fossil and nuclear plants to provide base-load generation capacity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design for safety for the Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway
abstract: The author discusses how risks were assessed and reduced to acceptable levels in the design of the Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway. Safety, reliability and security concepts are discussed. The author goes on to describe the design of the trains, stations, power supplies and fire prevention. Training and maintenance are also briefly described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution and utilisation of electrical power: a renaissance for the 21st century
abstract: The history of the electricity supply industry (ESI) of England and Wales is one of service to society. The supply engineers have ensured continuity of supply while improving efficiency and cost-effectiveness in the fields of distribution and utilisation. International growth in demand for energy is depleting the fossil-fuel reserves and damaging the environment. The author argues that the greater use of electricity to meet energy needs will result in better control of the environment and more efficient use of fuel. It is suggested that a co-ordinated drive is required from all sectors of power engineering to achieve this aim. Success will depend on the ready availability of electrical equipment and processes to enable society to use energy in an efficient and environmentally safe manner. The newly formed Public Electricity Supply Companies seem well placed to induce the co-ordination of all sectors of power engineering. The result could be a renaissance in the British power engineering industry with subsequent benefit to our economy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: China Light & Power's transmission system development practices
abstract: China Light & Power (CLP) is a Public Limited Company with responsibilities to its shareholders, the Hong Kong Government and the public at large in providing a secure, efficient and economical supply of electrical power to its supply area within the territory of Hong Kong. The author traces the history of CLP's transmission system developments over the past 40 years, which has been a period of vigorous and continuous growth and has produced some original engineering solutions to a range of unique problems encountered. Particular aspects of compact substation developments, within the densely populated Kowloon area, will be highlighted. A self-sufficient capability with a strong awareness of cost effectiveness have been central influencing factors in the development of the CLP system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
